Class MoreGatherers

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.collect.MoreGatherers
public final class MoreGatherers extends Object
Gatherers that Gatherers does not provide.

Gatherers exist since Java 24, so this class is only present when gaia runs on Java 24 or later: it lives in the META-INF/versions/24 part of the multi-release jar.

Like streams, the gatherers accept null elements, and the key functions may return null. Keys and elements are compared with Objects.equals(Object, Object).

In a parallel stream, instanceOf(Class), takeWhileInclusive(Predicate), takeLast(int), max(int, Comparator) and min(int, Comparator) run in parallel. The others depend on the elements before each one, so their stage runs sequentially, in encounter order.

  • Method Details

    • instanceOf

      public static <R> Gatherer<Object,?,R> instanceOf(Class<R> type)
      Returns a gatherer that keeps the elements that are instances of type, cast to it: a filter(type::isInstance) and a map(type::cast) in one step, with the right stream type. 
      Stream<Shape> shapes = ...;
Stream<Circle> circles = shapes.gather(MoreGatherers.instanceOf(Circle.class));

      Like the instanceof operator, it drops null elements.

      Type Parameters:
      R - the type to keep
      Parameters:
      type - the class of the type to keep
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the instances of type

    • distinctBy

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object, K extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,T> distinctBy(Function<? super T, ? extends K> key)
      Returns a gatherer that keeps the first element of each key, in encounter order. 
      Stream.of("apple", "avocado", "banana", "blueberry", "cherry")
        .gather(MoreGatherers.distinctBy(s -> s.charAt(0)))  // apple, banana, cherry

      It keeps every key it has seen until the stream ends.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      K - the type of the keys
      Parameters:
      key - the function that gives the key of an element
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the elements whose key was not seen before
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • takeWhileInclusive

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,T> takeWhileInclusive(Predicate<? super T> predicate)
      Returns a gatherer that keeps the elements while a predicate holds, and the first element that fails it, then stops. Unlike Stream.takeWhile(Predicate), the element that ends the run is kept, such as the terminator of a block. 
      Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5).gather(MoreGatherers.takeWhileInclusive(i -> i < 3))  // 1, 2, 3

      It stops pulling elements after the first that fails the predicate, so it ends an infinite stream.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      predicate - the predicate the elements before the last one satisfy
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the elements up to and including the first that fails predicate
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • groupRuns

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object, K extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,List<T>> groupRuns(Function<? super T, ? extends K> key)
      Returns a gatherer of the runs of consecutive elements with equal keys, each as an unmodifiable list. Unlike grouping, an element whose key appeared before, but not right before, starts a new run. 
      Stream.of("a1", "a2", "b1", "a3")
        .gather(MoreGatherers.groupRuns(s -> s.charAt(0)))  // [a1, a2], [b1], [a3]
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      K - the type of the keys
      Parameters:
      key - the function that gives the key of an element
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the runs of elements with equal keys
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • takeLast

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,T> takeLast(int n)
      Returns a gatherer that keeps the last n elements, or all of them if there are fewer. It holds at most n elements, and pushes them when the stream ends. 
      Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5).gather(MoreGatherers.takeLast(2))  // 4, 5

      With n of 0, it stops pulling elements at once, so it ends an infinite stream.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      n - the number of elements to keep
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the last n elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if n is negative
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • dropLast

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,T> dropLast(int n)
      Returns a gatherer that drops the last n elements, or all of them if there are fewer. It holds at most n elements, each pushed once n more have followed it. 
      Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5).gather(MoreGatherers.dropLast(2))  // 1, 2, 3
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      n - the number of elements to drop
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the elements but the last n
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if n is negative
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • max

      public static <T extends @Nullable Object> Gatherer<T,?,T> max(int n, Comparator<? super T> comparator)
      Returns a gatherer of the n greatest elements, the greatest first, or of all of them, sorted, if there are fewer. Equal elements keep their encounter order, and the earliest of them are kept when not all fit. It holds at most n elements, and pushes them when the stream ends. 
      Stream.of(3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2).gather(MoreGatherers.max(3, Comparator.naturalOrder()))  // 9, 5, 4

      An element that is not greater than the least of n kept ones costs one comparison. With n of 0, it stops pulling elements at once, so it ends an infinite stream.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      n - the number of elements to keep
      comparator - the order of the elements
      Returns:
      a gatherer of the n greatest elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if n is negative
      Since:
      0.1.2
